# Code of conduct

This project follows the [Contributor Covenant, version 2.1](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/1/code_of_conduct/). The summary below is binding; the full text fills any gap.

## Our pledge

We want taking part in this project to be free of harassment for everyone, whatever their age, body, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

## Expected behavior

- Be kind and respectful to other people.
- Respect different opinions and experiences.
- Give useful feedback, and accept it with grace.
- Take responsibility for your mistakes, apologize to the people they affected, and learn from them.
- Focus on what is best for the community, not only for yourself.

## Unacceptable behavior

- Sexual language or images, and sexual attention or advances of any kind.
- Trolling, insults, and personal or political attacks.
- Public or private harassment.
- Publishing someone's private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission.
- Other conduct that people would reasonably think is inappropriate in a professional setting.

## Scope

This code applies in every project space (issues, pull requests, discussions, the repository) and when someone represents the project in public.

## Reporting

Report a problem privately to the maintainer, [@dboeter](https://github.com/dboeter), through the repository's private reporting form: go to the [Security tab](https://github.com/dboeter/daily-diff/security) and click **Report a vulnerability**, then say in the title that it is a conduct report. You can also use GitHub's [report content](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/maintaining-your-safety-on-github/reporting-abuse-or-spam) option. The maintainer keeps the reporter's identity private.

## Enforcement

The maintainer decides what action fits, in this order of severity:

1. **Correction**: a private, written warning that explains what went wrong.
2. **Warning**: a warning with consequences, and no contact with the people involved for a set time.
3. **Temporary ban**: no interaction with the project for a set time.
4. **Permanent ban**: no interaction with the project, ever.
